questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding ‘Arthropoda’?

I. These animals are bilaterally symmetrical.

II. They have jointed legs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Both I and II__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Arthropoda:

 
 
• Arthropods have hard, **external shells called “exoskeletons,” segmented bodies, and jointed legs.**
 
• Some familiar examples are prawns, butterflies, houseflies, spiders, scorpions, and crabs.
 
• They exhibit an organ-system level of organization.
 
• They are** bilaterally symmetrical**, triploblastic, segmented and coelomate.
 
• The coelomic cavity is blood-filled.
 
• The body of arthropods is covered by chitinous.
 
• The body consists of a** head, thorax, and abdomen.**
 
• There is an open circulatory system, so the blood does not flow in well-defined blood vessels.
 
• Respiratory organs are the gills, book gills, book lungs, or tracheal system.
 
• Sensory organs like antennae, eyes (compound and simple), statocysts, or balance organs are present.
 
• Excretion takes place through malpighian tubules.
 
• Examples of Phylum Arthropoda are:
 
 
• Cockroach
 
• Prawn
 
• Crab
 
• Scorpion
 
• Centipede
 
• Housefly
 
• Ticks
 
• Mites

questions.question: Those organisms which take food synthesized by plants are called ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heterotrophs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Those organisms which take food synthesized by plants are called Heterotrophs.
 
• The term "heterotroph" includes organisms that cannot synthesize their own food and rely on complex organic substances for nutrition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phototrophic:**

 
 
• These are organisms that carry out photosynthesis to acquire energy.
 
• They utilize sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to produce glucose – their energy source.
 
• This group includes most plants and some bacteria and protists.
 
 
 
• **Autotrophs:**
 
 
• Autotrophs are organisms that can produce their own food from the substances available in their surroundings using light (photosynthesis) or chemical energy (chemosynthesis).
 
• Examples include plants, algae, and some types of bacteria.
 
 
 
• **Saprotrophs: **
 
 
• These are organisms that feed on dead and decaying organic matter by secreting enzymes into the environment and breaking down the organic matter into smaller particles which they then absorb.
 
• Fungi and bacteria are common examples of saprotrophs (also called saprophytes or decomposers).

questions.question: Amoeba pushes out one or more finger-like projections called ______ or false feet for movement and capture of food.

• It constantly changes its shape and position. 
 
• It pushes out one, or more finger-like projections, called pseudopodia or false feet for movement and capture of food.
 
• It feeds on some microscopic organisms. 
 
• When it senses food, it pushes out one or more finger-like projections **pseudopodia** around the food particle and engulfs it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
"There are holes or 'pores', all over the body. They are commonly called sponges, and are mainly found in marine habitats."

The above statement signifies which of the following phylum?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Porifera**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Phylum Porifera (*Porous *-pore; *ferre *- to bear)** includes the first and the most primitive group of multicellular animals, referred to as poriferans, i.e., pore-bearing animals.
 
• ​Phylum Porifera is an exclusive classification of aquatic animals.
 
• They are primitive, multicellular animals and are commonly called sponges.
 
• There are mostly marine and some are freshwater habitats, found in ponds and lakes.
 
• Its canal system is one of the most important features of sponges.
 
• A Canal system is a network of channels called Canals, which connect the spongocoel to the outside through Ostia.
 
• Digestion in animals of this Phylum is intracellular (inside collar cells) in nature.
 
• In Phylum Porifera, respiration occurs through the body surface by diffusion.
 
• Examples: *Sycon *(Scypha), *Spongilla *(Freshwater sponge), and *Euspongia* (Bath sponge)
 
• Sycon:
 
 
• These are solitary or colonial marine sponges found attached to rocks in shallow waters.
 
• The body is cylindrical in shape and covered in spores.
 
• Flagellated cells make up the radial canal. Water enters the body through the Ostia and travels to the radial canals via the prosopyles.
 
• These species reproduce in both sexual and asexual ways.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms can initiate ecological succession even in bare rocks?
questions.solution:

__
 
• Lichens are considered **pioneer species**, meaning they are among the first organisms to colonize bare rocks.
 
• Lichens secrete acids that slowly **break down rocks**, leading to the formation of soil, making it possible for other plants to grow.
 
• Lichens consist of fungi and algae (or cyanobacteria) living in a **symbiotic relationship**, allowing them to survive in harsh conditions.
 
• They are extremely** resilient** and can survive in extreme **environmental conditions**, such as high altitudes and exposed rock surfaces.
 
• **Soil formation:** By breaking down rock and accumulating organic material, lichens contribute to the creation of the first layer of soil.

• Orchids often grow on **other plants** (such as trees) without harming them, known as epiphytes, and are not capable of growing directly on bare rocks.
 
• Orchids typically appear in more advanced stages of **ecological succession** when the environment is more hospitable, with developed soil and host plants.
 
• They thrive in humid environments with specific light, moisture, and nutrient conditions, relying on **organic material** rather than barren environments.

**Aspergillus:**

 
• Aspergillus is a genus of **fungi **that decomposes organic matter and grows in a variety of environments, but it does not colonize bare rocks.
 
• This fungus breaks down already existing **organic matter**, such as dead plants or animals, and is more common in later stages of succession.
 
• Certain species of Aspergillus can cause **diseases** in plants and animals, including humans (e.g., aspergillosis in humans).

**Lily:**

 
• Lilies are **angiosperms** (flowering plants) that require a developed soil layer rich in nutrients, water, and light to grow.
 
• They appear in ecosystems where soil formation has already occurred, indicating that they are not **pioneer** species.
 
• Lilies grow in **wetlands** or well-drained, nutrient-rich soils and cannot survive in barren or rocky environments.

• **White blood cells** are of an amoeboid shape with a distinctive central membrane.
 
• The **amoeboid** shape of WBCs helps them to **squeeze out** through the **capillary wall**.
 
• White blood cells help in **defence mechanisms** for our body.
 
• They play a major role in** putting away foreign particles**.
 
• At the site of infection, white blood cells accumulate to **destroy pathogens.**
 
• Their **amoeboid shape** assists them to squeeze through blood capillaries and at the same time their pseudopodia help to kill pathogens by the process of phagocytosis. 
 
• They change their shape in order to **sink bacteria and separate invaders** in the body in order to protect the body against diseases and infections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png]

• **Nerve cells **(neurones) are 'excitable' cells which can transduce a variety of stimuli into electrical signals, continuously sending information about the external and internal environment (in the form of sequences of action potentials) to the central nervous system (CNS).
 
• **Guard cells** are pairs of epidermal cells that control gas diffusion by regulating the opening and closure of stomatal pores. Guard cells, like other types of plant cells, are surrounded by a three-dimensional, extracellular network of polysaccharide-based wall polymers.
 
• **Red blood cells **contain a protein called haemoglobin, which carries oxygen from the lungs to all parts of the body. Checking the number of red blood cells in the blood is usually part of a complete blood cell (CBC) test. A type of blood cell that is made in the bone marrow and found in the blood.

questions.question: The organisms that do not have a defined nucleus or organelles are classified in to ______ Kingdom.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Monera**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Monera kingdom:

 
 
• These organisms lack a defined nucleus or organelles and none of them has multicellular bodies.
 
• Some of them have cell walls while some do not.
 
• This group of species may either synthesize their own food (autotrophic) or obtain it from the environment (heterotrophic).
 
• Bacteria, blue-green algae (cyanobacteria), and mycoplasma are examples.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Fungi kingdom:

 
 
• These are heterotrophic eukaryotic organisms. 
 
• Some of them are known as saprotrophs, which feed on decaying organic matter.
 
• Others feed on the living protoplasm of a host organism. They are called parasites.
 
• Many of them have the capacity to become multicellular organisms at certain stages in their lives.
 
• Their cell walls are made of chitin, a tough complex sugar.
 
• Examples are yeasts, moulds, and mushrooms.
 
 
 
• **Protista** kingdom
 
 
• Protista kingdom single-celled eukaryotes.
 
• Characteristics of Protista are given bellow:
 
 
• Unicellular organism.
 
• Normally aquatic.
 
• Reproduction: Asexual & sexual.
 
• Well defined nucleus & membrane-bounded organelles.
 
 
 
• Group of Protista are given bellow:
 
 
• Prokaryotic: Dinoflagellate, Diatoms, Euglenoids.
 
• Consumer: Slime moulds, Myxomycetes.
 
• Protozoans: Slime moulds, Myxomycetes.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Plantae**
 
 
• Kingdom plantae includes all eukaryotic, chlorophyll-containing organisms called plants.
 
• Some of these members are primarily heterotrophic, such as insectivorous plants or parasites.
 
• Kingdom plantae is divided into 5 major divisions:
 
 
• Algae (Thallophyta)
 
• Bryophytes
 
• Pteridophytes
 
• Gymnosperms and
 
• Angiosperms
 
 
 
• 
 
Algae (Thallophyta)

 
 
• Algae are chlorophyll-containing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic and largely aquatic (both freshwater and marine) organisms.
 
• Algae are self-feeders.
 
• 
 
Bryophytes

 
 
• The bryophytes are generally classified into two main groups
 
• Liverworts
 
 
• Liverworts usually grow in moist, shady places such as banks of streams, marshy ground, damp soil, the bark of trees, and deep in the woods.
 
 
 
• Mosses
 
 
• Mosses grow in dense mats over moist shady places, especially during rainy seasons.
 
 
 
• 
 
Pteridophytes

 
 
• Pteridophytes are primitive seedless vascular plants also called cryptogams.
 
• The pteridophytes are found in cool, damp shady places though some may flourish well in sandy-soil conditions.
 
• 
 
Gymnosperms

 
 
• Gymnosperms are vascular plants having naked seeds.
 
• The gymnosperms are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilisation.
 
• 
 
Angiosperms

 
 
• Angiosperms are seed bearing plants or flowering plants.
 
• Unlike gymnosperms where the ovules are naked, in angiosperms the sporophylls are organized into flowers and seeds are produced inside fruits,

questions.question: Locomotion in ______ takes place with the help of a muscular foot.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Snails.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The snail is a very **slow-moving animal.**
 
• Like an **earthworm**, a snail too has a** liquid skeleton.**
 
• Snails have a** shell**, inside which they can hide to protect themselves from the heat of the sun and enemies.
 
• The shell is the **outer skeleton**, but it is **not made of bones**.
 
• For movement, **a thick structure and the head of the snail **come out of an opening in the shell.
 
• The thick structure is its** foot**, made of** strong muscles.**
 
• The** muscular foot produces wave-like movements** that push the **snail’s body forward.**
 
• A **trail of mucous** is left behind when the snail crawls.

 **Jellyfish**
 Jellyfish are animals of the phylum Cnidaria. They have no brain, heart, bones or eyes. They are made up of a smooth, bag-like body and tentacles armed with tiny, stinging cells.

 Sea urchins are the Class Echinoidea of the Phylum Echinodermata. These creatures are typically small, spiny, and round. They live in all the earth’s oceans, at depths ranging from the tide line to 15,000 feet.

 Earthworms are classified in the phylum Annelida or Annelids. They are the main contributors to enriching and improving soil for plants, animals and even humans.

questions.question: In the animal kingdom, which of the following phyla includes animals with a segmented body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Annelida**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Annelida is a phylum of segmented worms, which includes earthworms, leeches, and marine worms.
 
• Members of the Annelida phylum have bodies divided into repetitive segments called metameres.
 
• This segmentation allows for greater flexibility and mobility, facilitating burrowing and other locomotive behaviors.
 
• Annelids possess a true coelom, a body cavity completely lined with mesoderm, which aids in the function of their hydrostatic skeleton.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Metamerism:** This refers to the segmentation of the body into a series of repeated units, which is a key characteristic of Annelida.
 
• **Closed Circulatory System:** Annelids have a closed circulatory system, meaning that blood is enclosed within blood vessels and is pumped by a heart.
 
• **Setae:** Many annelids possess small bristle-like structures called setae on each segment, which help in locomotion and anchorage.
 
• **Ecological Role:** Annelids play a significant role in soil health as decomposers and by aerating the soil, which is vital for plant growth.
 
• **Clitellum:** In earthworms, a thickened, glandular section of the body known as the clitellum secretes mucus during reproduction, aiding in the transfer of sperm and the formation of a cocoon for the developing embryos.

questions.question: Which of the following classes includes the family of turtles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reptilia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Turtles belong to the class **Reptilia**, which also includes snakes, lizards, and crocodiles.
 
• Reptiles are characterized by their **cold-blooded metabolism**, scaly skin, and the laying of eggs with leathery shells.
 
• Turtles have a distinctive feature known as a **shell**, which is developed from their ribs and acts as a shield.
 
• Most reptiles, including turtles, are **ectothermic** (rely on external sources of temperature to regulate their body heat).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chondrichthyes**

 
 
• Chondrichthyes is a class that includes **cartilaginous fishes** such as sharks, rays, and skates.
 
• These fishes have a skeleton made of cartilage rather than bone.
 
• They are characterized by having paired fins, paired nostrils, scales, a heart with its chambers in series, and skeletons made of cartilage.
 
 
 
• **Amphibia**
 
 
• Amphibia is a class that includes **amphibians** such as frogs, toads, salamanders, and newts.
 
• Amphibians are characterized by their ability to live both in water and on land.
 
• They have a life cycle that includes both an aquatic larval stage and a terrestrial adult stage.
 
• Amphibians have moist, permeable skin that assists in respiration.
 
 
 
• **Aves**
 
 
• Aves is a class that includes **birds**.
 
• Birds are characterized by their feathers, beaks, and laying of hard-shelled eggs.
 
• They have a high metabolic rate, a four-chambered heart, and a lightweight but strong skeleton.
 
• Most birds are capable of flight, though some species are flightless.

questions.question: What cells help In osmoregulation In platyhelminthes?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Flame cells** are specialized cells that form** part of the excretory system** in these organisms, known as **protonephridia.**
 
• Flame cells play a primary** role in osmoregulation,** the process by which a balance of water and ions is maintained within the body.
 
• Along with osmoregulation, flame cells also help in the **removal of waste products**.
 
• This system is not only found in Platyhelminthes but **also in other types of flatworms and invertebrates**. However, it is most prominent in **Platyhelminthes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nerve cells:**

 
 
• Platyhelminthes have a decentralized nerve cell network and two longitudinal nerve cords running along their body length.
 
• These nerve cells, also known as **neurons**, are responsible for **transmitting signals** across the organism.
 
• They enable **sensing the environment and coordinating the organism's **response to it.
 
 
 
• **Ganglia:**
 
 
• Ganglia are simple forms of** "brains"** or collections of nerve cell bodies that process information in invertebrates such as **Platyhelminthes**.
 
• They serve as the **central nervous system** in these organisms, acting as control centres that coordinate nerve signals.
 
 
 
• **Hooks:**
 
 
• Some Platyhelminthes, specifically parasitic ones, have **hooks and suckers**.
 
• These structures are **not cells, **but adaptations that help the worm to attach to the host's tissue.
 
• The hooks **assist in anchoring the parasite** to its host and facilitate the feeding process.

questions.question: Which of the following can be a basis of difference between a salamander and a house-wall lizard apart from their habitat?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Salamanders** have smooth, moist skin without scales, which helps in cutaneous respiration (breathing through the skin).
 
• **House-wall lizards** possess dry, scaly skin that protects them from desiccation and provides a barrier against predators.
 
• The **absence of scales** in salamanders allows them to live in moist environments, whereas the presence of scales in lizards allows them to thrive in drier habitats.
 
• Scales in lizards are made of keratin, providing structural strength and aiding in locomotion by reducing friction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cold-blooded Nature:**

 
 
• Both salamanders and lizards are ectothermic (cold-blooded), meaning they rely on external sources to regulate their body temperature.
 
 
 
• **Egg-laying Feature:**
 
 
• Both groups generally lay eggs, though some salamanders can give birth to live young depending on the species.
 
 
 
• **Heart Structure:**
 
 
• Both salamanders and lizards typically have a three-chambered heart, consisting of two atria and one ventricle.
 
 
 
• **Skin Function:**
 
 
• Salamander skin helps in respiration, whereas lizard skin primarily protects against environmental hazards.
 
 
 
• **Habitat Differences:**
 
 
• Salamanders prefer moist or aquatic environments, while lizards are more commonly found in terrestrial or arid regions.

questions.question: Identify an example of organisms that are free-swimming and bottom-dwelling forms.
questions.solution:

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**Zooplankton:

__
 
• Zooplankton is the common name given to many small species of animals found in fresh and marine waters throughout the world.
 
• The word zooplankton, derived from Greek, means "wandering animals."
 
• They float in the water column and drift with the currents. Most of these animals are so minute they are visible only with a microscope, although some species can reach lengths of eight feet.
 
• Two general groups of zooplankton exist those that remain planktonic throughout their entire life (holoplankton), and those that are larval stages of larger life forms (meroplankton).

• Derived from the Greek words phyto (plant) and plankton (made to wander or drift), phytoplankton are microscopic organisms that live in watery environments, both salty and fresh. 
 
• Some phytoplankton are bacteria, some are protists, and most are single-celled plants.
 
• Among the common kinds are cyanobacteria, silica-encased diatoms, dinoflagellates, green algae, and chalk-coated coccolithophores.
